replacement.title: test(maintenance): prove and document the foundation
replacement.body:
Part of maintenance foundation #1472. The operator authorized direct-issue implementation of this foundation scope; the withdrawn `maintenance-jobs/001` plan is historical.

## Goal

One compiled core binary demonstrates storage, installation, bounded
execution, and monitoring across two fixture repositories.

## Scope

Reuse the preceding package/conformance suites in one hermetic
install/run/status/uninstall flow. Inject clock, cron, fake harness processes,
and temporary bare remotes. Cover supported Darwin/Linux arm64/amd64 builds
and core upgrade/convergence ownership. Document jobs CRUD API, CLI use,
published policy, daily deduplication, timezone limits, audit lookup, disable,
uninstall, retained work, and unsupported-delivery refusal.

Keep this work in the existing root Go module and the installed core `pyxis` binary. Repository policy remains `.pyxis/maintenance/jobs.yaml`; lifecycle audit output belongs in ignored `.pyxis/maintenance/logs.jsonl`, with detailed execution diagnostics under ignored `.pyxis/logs/maintenance/`.

Installed maintenance CLI, jobs API, existing harness conformance,
core ownership/release contracts, and operator runbook. **Excluded:** Live model
inference, actual host cron activation, real CI jobs, migration, rubric evaluation,
or describing inherited CI/adoption DoD rows as completed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One binary handles two fixture repositories without cross-repository mutation; a generic test-only job launches through each existing adapter and records its outcome.
- [ ] No-op reinstall, competing claims, timeout/cancellation, drift, audit failure, and policy-independent uninstall pass.
- [ ] Upgrade/convergence preserves jobs and journal; release payload omits local logs.
- [ ] Applicable repository checks pass under current AGENTS.md without the race detector.
- [ ] The runbook accurately states excluded capabilities.

## Dependencies

#1496. Each blocker must be merged and closed before this issue is dispatched; closed-as-not-planned work is not an implemented prerequisite.

## Execution bounds and reuse

- Use the existing pinned YAML library, native harness registry/routing/runtime, Git-ref CAS transport, and core CLI seams where this unit needs them. Prefer the standard library; no new module or parallel implementation of those mechanisms.
- Limit this issue to at most 280 added production logic lines (function lines excluding blank/comment/standalone-brace lines and type/import/data declarations). Report total diff separately. If the exact behavior cannot fit, stop with a concrete bounded change proposal.
- Run only this issue in its own executor-owned checkout from current main, with a 60-minute worker bound, the existing repair limits, required repository checks, and configured independent review. No race-detector run. Publication requires verified checks; approval and merge remain human.
- Add no semantic memory for routine implementation or verification. Preserve useful outcomes in the owning issue/PR and keep local diagnostics ignored.

## Out of scope

A specific CI job or prompt; CI timing/evidence adapters or optimization; PR publication; legacy CI migration/adoption; new shared sandbox or credential protocols; report/export pipelines; a janitor; notifications or automatic merges; crash recovery, retries, takeover, catch-up, or non-daily scheduling.
